validation.notes: Repaired packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts: recoverToolInvocation now replays a replay-safety-matched ('safe' call + 'safe' tool) effect only when the drive is not cancelled, so cancellation wins over retransfer. A cancelled recovery therefore never clears the durable replay checkpoint (clearReplayCheckpoint is skipped), never issues a tool invocation, and instead reads the checkpoint and publishes interruptedOutcome (checkpoint content + INTERRUPTION_MARKER, details/usage preserved, isError true, terminate false). Non-cancelled safe/safe calls still clear, invoke exactly once, and settle the outcome after the effect completes. Validation drove the real recoverToolInvocation through the read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs helper (only checkpoint IO, tool execution and outcome publication are boundary fakes) with 5 assertion groups / 24 assertions: cancelled safe/safe (no clear, no invoke, exactly one publish, interrupted evidence with durable snapshot and marker), repeated cancelled runs, one-sided replay safety (safe/never, never/safe, safe/no-policy, safe/absent tool), non-cancelled safe/safe (event order clear->invoke->effect-complete->publish, single invoke, non-error effect result), and non-cancelled unsafe call. Cross-realm VM message objects were normalized into the host realm (JSON round-trip) before deepStrictEqual rather than loosening assertions. Negative control: temporarily reverting the identical one-line guard to 'if (call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe")' (verified exactly 1 replacement) made the regression exit 1 with AssertionError 'cancelled recovery must not clear the replay checkpoint' and event diff [clear, invoke, effect-complete, publish] vs [read, publish]; the fix was then restored and the regression re-run green (exit 0). No dependencies or network were installed; only Node 24's built-in TypeScript stripping and node:vm were used, with the harmless ExperimentalWarning notices on stderr. No optional validation dependency (e.g. tsc/vitest, which need node_modules) was available, so the VM regression script was the focused validation.
